title: Battle of Red Mountain
text: The Battle of Red Mountain was the climactic battle of the War of the First Council, and resulted in the sudden disappearance of the entire Dwemer race from Nirn.[18][16] The battle was fought at Red Mountain in Resdayn (present-day Morrowind) around 1E 700[19] (or possibly earlier),[nb 1] between the Chimer (led by General Nerevar, the Hortator) and the Dwemer (led by Dumac Dwarfking),[16][20] along with armies of Nords and Orcs.[17][21] The exact truth of what happened cannot be determined due to conflicting accounts,[22] but all agree that by the time the dust settled, much of that dust was all that remained of the Dwemer.[16] Though Nerevar died, his people claimed victory, and four Chimer were positioned to become living gods.[18][16] The First Council was held together for hundreds of years thanks to the friendship between Dumac and Nerevar. However, through means lost to history, Lord Voryn Dagoth of House Dagoth learned of a Dwemer scheme: deep in the bowels of Red Mountain on the island of Vvardenfell, the Dwemer had found the Heart of Lorkhan, and High Craftlord Kagrenac planned to harness it and use it to power a giant mechanical god.[18][16][23] Lord Dagoth reported this to the Chimer leadership, and eventually, the Hortator Nerevar confirmed it with his patron Azura. Nerevar confronted his friend Dumac, and they quarreled bitterly (some sources assert Dumac did not know of Kagrenac's plan at the time and thus misunderstood Nerevar's concerns). As a result, Nerevar led the Chimer to war in order to stop this profane usurpation.[18][16] At the start of the war, Dwemeri forces were concentrated in the northwest of the province, and their campaign initially had great success throughout the north.[17][24] There is speculation that many of the great metal automatons the Dwemer used as troops in the battle were built in the Great Workshops of Nchardak on the island of Solstheim. The coastal Dwemeri city was reputedly able to produce one automaton a day, an apparently impressive rate of production.[25] Many outlanders were at the battle, notably Orcs and Nords, and sources often designate them as allies of the Dwemer.[17] Nerevar, meanwhile, led his united people, the nomadic Ashlanders as well as the Great Houses (House Redoran, in particular, likes to trumpet its substantial contribution of warriors to the battle).[17][26][27] Nerevar did not have full control of the Chimer forces until a series of defeats convinced the Great Houses to relinquish command.[24] Once he had full command of the Chimer forces, Nerevar carefully orchestrated a confrontation at Dumac's citadel, a great Dwemer stronghold within Red Mountain where the Heart was being kept.[17][2] The bulk of Nerevar's troops left Narsis and headed north at roughly the same time as a horde of westerners entered Morrowind from the west and began crossing the Inner Sea.[18][21] Some sources claim that all who opposed Nerevar's forces in the battle were exterminated.[17][24] Others state that while all enemies of the Chimer forces were decisively defeated, only the Dwemer were wiped out completely.[28]

title: Numidium
text: Numidium,[1] also known as Anumidium, Anumidum, the Brass God, the Prime Gestalt,[2] NM,[3] the Brass Tower,[4] Walk-Brass,[5][UOL 1] Big Walker,[6][2] Walking Star,[7] and the Divine Skin,[2] was a colossal construct of Dwemer origin.[8] It was constructed by Dwemeri Tonal Architect Lord Kagrenac[9][10][11] to be a new god, powered by the Heart of Lorkhan,[12] made to retake Resdayn from the Chimer[13] and possibly to make the Dwemer race immortal.[11] The Dwemer vanished from Tamriel before the Brass God could be activated, though their disappearance may be directly related to this endeavor.[11] The Numidium was, in practice, a weapon of devastating power. A 'thousand foot tall automaton, a golem or an atronach[nb 1] of sorts', it was used by Emperor Tiber Septim to complete his conquest of Tamriel at the end of the Second Era, but was destroyed afterward.[14] The golem was rebuilt and reactivated centuries later, and became the center of the phenomenon known as the Warp in the West, after which it was destroyed again.[8] Temporal distortions have accompanied each known use of the Numidium,[6] to the point that the Warp in the West is sometimes known as the 'Second Numidian Effect'.[15] Some believe that the Numidium was intrinsically evil: a ranking Clockwork Apostle refered to it as the 'most profane' of the Dwemer's creations, a 'walking horror', the 'Antipodal-God-Thing that reigned on the darkest pole of the sacred Nirn-Sphere', and the 'welded knot at the center of Anu that must be untied. The Apostles considered the Numidium the greatest threat to Sotha Sil's goals of bringing about the Nirn-Ensuing and the Anuic convergence of Anuvanna'si. Indeed, in the Second Era, the Clockwork City's supervising Factotum, Aios, would name Numidium first among the existential threats to the City.[16][3] A second Numidium, Akulakhan, was partially constructed in Morrowind in the late Third Era by Dagoth Ur. However, the destruction of Kagrenac's enchantments on the Heart of Lorkhan in 3E 427 prevented its activation

title: The Warp in the West — Overview
text:
Era: 3E 417 (9th to 11th of Frostfall)
Location: Iliac Bay (High Rock + Hammerfell)
Type: Localized Dragon Break / Second Numidian Effect / “Miracle of Peace”

The Warp in the West was a reality- and time-distortion event localized to the Iliac Bay. It began between the 9th and 11th of Frostfall, 3E 417, after political conflict surrounding the death of King Lysandus of Daggerfall escalated into a struggle for control of the Totem of Tiber Septim. The Totem could control Numidium, the ancient Dwemer brass golem once used by Tiber Septim. 

During the Warp, multiple major powers (Sentinel, Wayrest, Daggerfall, Orsinium, and even the Emperor) somehow all gained control of Numidium and used it to consolidate power at the same time. Before the event, the Iliac Bay contained forty-four city-states; after the strange cataclysms, only four major kingdoms remained: Sentinel, Wayrest, Daggerfall, and Orsinium—each swearing loyalty to the Emperor.

The Warp is sometimes compared to the Middle Dawn Dragon Break, but its effects appear to have been confined primarily to the Iliac Bay region.

title: The Warp in the West — Numidium, Totem, and Mantella
text:
Key artifacts: Numidium, Totem of Tiber Septim, Mantella

Numidium was a colossal Dwemer automaton later used by Emperor Tiber Septim to conquer Tamriel. To operate Numidium, two legendary components were central:
- The Totem of Tiber Septim: used to control Numidium.
- The Mantella: a massive gem that served as Numidium’s power source by holding the “heart” (life force) of a powerful individual.

According to a commonly told account, Zurin Arctus (Tiber Septim’s Battlemage) helped create these artifacts and, by some versions of the legend, used his own heart to power the Mantella. After Tamriel was united, Arctus supposedly objected to further use of Numidium and attempted to reclaim his heart. In the attempt, both he and Numidium were destroyed, and the Totem and Mantella were lost. Unable to truly die without his heart, Arctus became the undead figure known as the Underking.

Over centuries, the Blades worked to find and reassemble Numidiums remains. By 3E 401, the Totem was known to be in the possession of Lord Woodborne of Wayrest, and the Mantellas location was later divined.

title: The Warp in the West — Lead-up and the Totem Bidding War
text:
Lead-up trigger: Death of King Lysandus of Daggerfall; struggle for Totem ownership

In 3E 403, King Lysandus of Daggerfall was assassinated (not immediately understood as assassination). In 3E 405, Emperor Uriel Septim VII sent an agent of the Blades to investigate events in the region. The investigation concluded that Lord Woodborne was responsible for Lysandus’ death as part of a scheme to seize power. 

The Blades agent recovered the Totem of Tiber Septim from Woodborne’s co-conspirator Gothryd (Lysandus’ son and the new King of Daggerfall). Once the Totem was back in play, the powers of the Iliac Bay made competing offers for it, effectively turning the Totem into the centerpiece of a high-stakes political contest.

A major danger surrounded the Totem: Zurin Arctus placed a seal on it such that only certain “worthy” individuals or crowned heads could wield it safely; others risked death if they attempted to activate Numidium.

title: The Warp in the West — The Seven Claimants
text:
Claimants: Seven major powers deemed “worthy” to contend for the Totem

Seven “worthy” claimants emerged as potential users of the Totem of Tiber Septim:

1) Sentinel (Queen Akorithi): sought dominance in the Iliac Bay by destroying rivals.
2) Wayrest (King Eadwyre and Queen Barenziah): sought to defeat enemies and consolidate power.
3) Daggerfall (King Gothryd): sought dominance in the Iliac Bay by destroying rivals.
4) Mannimarco, King of Worms: desired the Mantella’s power for personal apotheosis rather than merely Numidium’s military might.
5) The Underking: sought to reclaim his lost heart (linked to the Mantella) to finally achieve true death.
6) Gortwog gro-Nagorm (Orcish warlord): sought to restore an Orcish homeland (Orsinium) and gain recognition/equality for Orcs.
7) Emperor Uriel Septim VII and the Blades (via agents such as Lady Brisienna): sought to use Numidium to pacify the region and restore Imperial order in High Rock and Hammerfell.

A mysterious Blades-associated figure (often described as an unknown hero/adventurer) recovered the Mantella from Aetherius and set the stage for Numidiums activation.

title: The Warp in the West — The 9th of Frostfall and Dragon Break Effects
text:
Date window: 9th to 11th of Frostfall, 3E 417
Core anomaly: contradictory outcomes; time distortions; catastrophic battles and disasters

What occurred during the Warp is unclear because reports are contradictory and paradoxical; many Blades agents were lost. Investigations concluded no fully coherent historical account could be formed—only that a “miracle” occurred. A recurring claim is that each of the seven powers took ownership of the Totem simultaneously and achieved their goals to some degree, implying time fractured into overlapping outcomes.

Some observers experienced the three days as merged into one with missing time; other events seemed to take far longer than three days could contain. Natural disasters devastated the region: earthquakes, freak sandstorms in the Alikr, fires, and tsunamis along the Bjoulsae River.

Reports describe multiple titanic battles taking place around the Iliac Bay “simultaneously,” including clashes involving Orsinium, Wayrest, and Daggerfall in areas such as Gavaudon, Daenia, and the Ilessan Hills. The scale of destruction included firestorms that ignited forests and widespread decimation.

Wayrest’s court later implied they knew an ancient weapon would be activated and had attempted to buy it from a young adventurer, but when attacks began, they responded by sending armies—whose rapid travel and timing remain unexplained.

title: The Warp in the West — Aftermath and the “Miracle of Peace”
text:
Result: 44 states → 4 kingdoms; Imperial loyalty; long-term political stabilization

In the immediate geopolitical aftermath, the Iliac Bay changed from forty-four independent regions to four major kingdoms—Daggerfall, Sentinel, Wayrest, and Orsinium—separated by blackened, desolate borderlands. Although smaller clashes continued for months, they were minor compared to the power unleashed during the Warp.

In later years the event was also called the “Miracle of Peace,” because despite immense death and destruction, the end state was a more stable Iliac Bay that remained loyal to the Empire. By 3E 433, the rulers of the four kingdoms were described as “ordained by the Nine,” and many Bretons interpreted the event as divine restoration—though the Blades strongly doubted a divine origin.

Key consequences attributed to specific claimants:
- Sentinel expanded along the northern coast of Hammerfell; after Queen Akorithis death, her son Lhotun ruled with reverence for Yokudan heritage and respect for Imperial ways.
- Gortwogs Orsinium (often called Nova Orsinium) gained Imperial recognition, and Orcish citizens became more integrated across the Empire.
- Mannimarco used the Totem/Mantella-related power to achieve apotheosis; in later years the Necromancers Moon was believed by his followers to embody his ascension.
- Numidium vanished from Tamriel, and the Underking was not seen again. Some rumors claim the Underking reclaimed his heart, was annihilated along with Numidium, and created a wide anti-magic zone—though the exact location is unknown.
- The mysterious Blades-associated agent/hero who found the Totem also disappeared amid the chaos.

title: Indoril Nerevar — Early Life
text: Nerevars early life is mostly preserved through myth and conflicting traditions. Legends associate him with the “moon-and-star” symbol: some say he was born under a moon-and-star, others that he bore a moon-and-star birthmark, and some that his family standard carried the moon-and-star. Vivecs account frames Nerevar as of the same generation as Dagoth Ur and older than the Tribunal, and suggests he worked as a protector for a merchant caravan. During the late First Era, the Nords used armies and the thu’um to dominate Resdayn; after the War of Succession weakened them, Nerevar moved to seize the moment for rebellion.

title: Indoril Nerevar — The Hortator and the First Council
text:
Nerevar united disparate Chimer factions and became Hortator (their collective war leader). His alliance with the Dwemer was essential because Nordic power had not subdued Dwemeri underground cities; the alliance relied heavily on Nerevars personal bond with Dumac. Together, they repulsed the Nords at Red Mountain in 1E 416 and maintained cooperation for centuries. Dumac attended Nerevars wedding to Almalexia and gifted the swords Hopesfire and Trueflame (Trueflame becoming known as the Blade of Nerevar). Nerevar and Dumac later attended Emperor Gorieuss coronation as Resdayns representatives.

Key relationships: Sotha Sil served as teacher/adviser; Vivec was a junior counselor; Voryn Dagoth was Lord High Councilor of House Dagoth (often described as loyal); Alandro Sul was Nerevars shield-companion. Traditions also describe Nerevar as Azuras champion: Azura blessed the Moon-and-Star ring so it would kill any wearer except Nerevar, and he swore to honor Ashlander ways, earning their allegiance.

title: Indoril Nerevar — Vivecs Lessons and Mythic Deeds
text: Accounts in The 36 Lessons of Vivec place many mythic episodes during the era of the First Council. These stories portray extraordinary journeys and feats attributed to Nerevar and Vivec, including travel to distant lands and metaphysical teachings (e.g., claims about CHIM), as well as symbolic battles and pilgrimages described in vivid, allegorical language.

title: Indoril Nerevar — War of the First Council Prelude
text: Voryn Dagoth learned of Kagrenacs plan to exploit the Heart of Lorkhan, which the Chimer would consider blasphemous. Dagoth warned Nerevar; when Nerevar confronted Dumac, the alliance fractured. Some sources suggest misunderstanding, implying Dumac may not have known the full plan until late. As war loomed, Nerevar again had to unify Chimer factions under his leadership. Despite Chimer skill in arms and magic, Dwemer technology made them a terrifying force, and the Chimer suffered defeats until they regrouped under Nerevar.

title: Indoril Nerevar — Battle of Red Mountain and the Dwemer Disappearance
text: Nerevar orchestrated a climactic confrontation at Red Mountain using strategy and Ashlander scouts. The battle was a decisive Chimer victory but cost many lives, including Nerevars; his sword Trueflame was shattered and its fragments lost. The disappearance of the Dwemer is explained differently across traditions: Tribunal Temple teachings claim Nerevar (with Azura and the Tribunal) used the Heart of Lorkhan to make the Dwemer vanish, while other accounts hold the Dwemer destroyed themselves. Sources conflict regarding House Dagoths role and whether Voryn Dagoth remained loyal.

title: Indoril Nerevar — Contested Accounts of His Death
text: How Nerevar died at Red Mountain is heavily disputed. Nordic traditions claim he was mortally wounded by Lorkhan and then feigned death to cut out the Heart and defeat the God of Mortals. Vivecs narrative implies Nerevar died from wounds received late in the battle, potentially involving Dumac and possibly Dagoth Ur. Ashlander belief holds that the Tribunal, seeking the Hearts power, poisoned a wounded Nerevar; this accusation is linked to Alandro Suls allegations after he was reportedly blinded and later lived among the Ashlanders.

title: Indoril Nerevar — Legacy, Oath, and Azuras Curse
text:
After Red Mountain, Nerevar insisted that Almalexia, Sotha Sil, and Vivec swear before Azura never to use Kagrenacs Tools in the profane way intended by the Dwemer. Later, the Tribunal broke this oath and used the Tools to take divine power; Azura appeared and cursed them, declaring that her champion Nerevar would return to punish their betrayal and that the Chimer would become Dunmer, sharing the Tribunals fate.

The dispute over Nerevars death and the Tribunals legitimacy created a long-lasting schism: Great Houses accepted the Tribunal as living gods, while Ashlanders condemned them as murderers and preserved older traditions. Cultural/iconographic legacy includes masks and Ordinator vestments depicting Nerevars visage, and some traditions even claim he was transformed into a Bonewalker and depicted that way on Temple shrines.

title: Almalexia — Origins and Early Rule
text: Little is known of Almalexia before she became the wife of Indoril Nerevar. Temple myth claims that on Mount Assarnibibi, Molag Bal oversaw the ninety nine lovers of Boethiah who gave birth to her. She hailed from one of the Great Houses of Morrowind. Early in her life she ruled the capital city of Mournhold as queen. She operated an orphanage and commanded an orphan legion. She also led a faction known as the Shouts who carried out her will.

title: Almalexia — Formation of the First Council
text: Almalexia, also known as Ayem, played a central role in the formation of the First Council. Vivec emerged from a prophetic egg image delivered to her by Nerevar. Alongside Nerevar, Vivec, and Sotha Sil, she formed an alliance with the Dwemer to repel Nordic occupation. The Chimer and Dwemer defeated Nordic chieftains including Hoag Merkiller and Ysmir Wulfharth. After victory, the First Council was established. Almalexia wed Nerevar and received the twin blades Hopesfire and Trueflame from Dumac. Nerevar ruled as Hortator with Almalexia as queen.

title: Almalexia — War of the First Council and Red Mountain
text: The fall of the First Council culminated in the Battle of Red Mountain. Accounts differ. In Ashlander tradition, the Tribunal betrayed Nerevar after he refused to use Kagrenac tools for divine power. The Tribunal allegedly murdered him using poison and ritual deception. Vivec denies this version and claims Nerevar died of battle wounds. Nordic accounts describe the involvement of Shor and Wulfharth. In all versions, the Dwemer vanished and Nerevar died.

title: Almalexia — Ascension and Azura Curse
text: After Red Mountain, Sotha Sil learned how to use Kagrenac tools to tap into the Heart of Lorkhan. The Tribunal traveled to the Heart Chamber and became living gods known as Almsivi. Azura cursed them and transformed the Chimer into Dunmer, turning their skin ash gray and eyes red. Azura declared Nerevar would return to punish them. Almalexia viewed the transformation as a blessing of divine protection rather than a curse.

title: Almalexia — Role as Living Goddess
text: As a living god, Almalexia ruled Morrowind alongside Vivec and Sotha Sil. Resdayn became Morrowind. The Tribunal Temple dominated political and religious life. Almalexia was associated with midday mercy and served as patron of House Indoril. She commanded the Hands of Almalexia as her personal guard. She performed miracles, healed Corprus sufferers, inspired saints, and defended Morrowind from threats including Mehrunes Dagon and Akaviri invasions.

title: Almalexia — Decline During Dagoth Ur Return
text: When Dagoth Ur awoke in 2E 882, he severed the Tribunal from the Heart of Lorkhan. Their divine power began to fade. The Great Ghostfence was built to contain him. The loss of Kagrenac tools Sunder and Keening weakened the Tribunal further. Almalexia grew harsher and withdrew from public life. Tension grew between her and Vivec. Her divinity diminished without access to the Heart.

title: Almalexia — Madness and Death
text:
As her divine power faded after losing access to the Heart of Lorkhan, Almalexia changed dramatically. Those few who still saw her observed that she no longer acted as the compassionate Lady of Mercy, but more as a hardened warrior queen. Those closest to her understood that she had become obsessed with preserving her divine image at any cost.

In place of fading godhood, she relied on ancient relics and Dwemer machinery to maintain fear and control. She used tonal devices to shroud Mournhold in ash storms, punishing her people for what she believed was failing faith. Her paranoia deepened into a singular goal: to become the one true god of the Dunmer, eliminating all rivals and uniting Morrowind under absolute authority.

After the fall of Dagoth Ur in 3E 427, the Nerevarine arrived in Mournhold. Seeing him as both threat and opportunity, Almalexia devised a calculated scheme. She traveled to the Clockwork City and murdered Sotha Sil. She then unleashed mechanical constructs into Mournhold in order to frame him and position herself as savior.

She lured the Nerevarine into the Clockwork City, hoping the mechanical defenses would destroy him. When he survived, she confronted him directly. In battle, her remaining divine strength failed her. She was slain by the Nerevarine within the Clockwork City.

In her final moments she called Vivec a fool. Vivec, the last remaining Tribune, expressed sorrow rather than anger and later retrieved her body. He interred both Almalexia and Sotha Sil in proper Velothi fashion.

Azura later declared that Almalexia death was a boon for Morrowind, claiming the Lady of Mercy would have betrayed the Dunmer as she had betrayed those closest to her. By 3E 432, Imperial reports stated that Almalexia, Dagoth Ur, Sotha Sil, and possibly Vivec were destroyed in what was termed the Nerevarine fury, and that the Nerevarine himself had vanished.

title: Almalexia — Continued Worship and Legacy
text: After her death, many Dunmer continued to believe she still lived. Over time the New Temple declared Tribunal worship misguided and restored reverence to the Reclamations including Boethiah. Some sects continued secret worship of Almalexia, including a hidden cult on Solstheim that built a statue in her honor. Though no longer worshiped as a living god, she is remembered as a saint of Dunmeri history.

title: Almalexia — Alandro Sul Account of Red Mountain and Nerevar Death
text:
Alandro Sul, a shield companion of Nerevar who later lived among the Ashlanders, gave an account of events surrounding the War of the First Council and the Battle of Red Mountain. In his telling, Voryn Dagoth brought proof to Nerevar and the Tribunal that Kagrenac, the Dwemer high engineer, had discovered the Heart of Lorkhan and was using special tools to draw power from it in order to create a new god, the Numidium. Ayem, Almalexia, and the rest of the Tribunal urged war against the Dwemer for this sacrilege.

While the Tribunal fought Dwemer forces in the open, Nerevar and Voryn Dagoth infiltrated the Heart Chamber. There they slew King Dumac and Kagrenac, but Dumac inflicted grievous wounds on Nerevar. Nerevar then summoned Azura, who taught Nerevar and Voryn how to use Kagrenac tools to sever the Heart power from the Dwemer. The Dwemer then turned to dust and disappeared as a people. Voryn Dagoth advised destroying the tools because of the danger they represented, but Nerevar chose to consult the Tribunal first.

According to Sul, the Tribunal counseled Nerevar to use the tools to claim Resdayn and potentially the whole world for the Chimer. Nerevar was disturbed by this ambition and intended to summon Azura again. The Tribunal, now greedy for the Heart power, feigned the Azura summoning ritual and murdered Nerevar using poisoned ritual elements. In this version, Almalexia used poison candles, Sotha Sil used poisoned robes, and Vivec used poisoned invocations. Other imagined versions of the murder describe Vivec impaling Nerevar with Muatra, Sotha Sil severing his face, and Almalexia severing his feet.

title: Almalexia — The Three in One and Almsivi Rule of Morrowind
text:
After Red Mountain, Almsivi became the god kings of the Dunmer and reshaped society. The name Resdayn was replaced and the province became known as Morrowind. Of the seven Great Houses associated with the First Council era, the legacies of House Dwemer and House Dagoth were erased by Almsivi. The Grand Council continued with five houses, but the Tribunal Temple became the dominant power in Morrowind.

Each Living God had a city dedicated to their worship, with alternate names used to distinguish the city from the deity who resided within it. Almalexia was associated with Mournhold, Sotha Sil with the Clockwork City, and Vivec with Vivec City. Each also maintained an honor guard: the Hands of Almalexia served Almalexia, the Clockwork Apostles served Sotha Sil, and the Buoyant Armigers served Vivec.

The Tribunes were also linked to Great Houses in temperament and sympathy. Almalexia aligned most closely with House Indoril and its secure serenity. Sotha Sil was associated with the unconventional and iconoclastic disposition of House Telvanni. Vivec was associated with House Redoran and its focus on creeds and deeds. They were further symbolized as times of day: Sotha Sil as the morning sun, Almalexia as midday mercy, and Vivec as a star spun night.

In Vivec sermon based metaphysics, Ayem is described as the Mother, active and clawed like a nix hound, and portrayed as a key force in the fate of Morrowind and the splendor of the stars. Vivec is often described as the most public and popular Tribune, especially on Vvardenfell, though some accounts claim Almalexia was the most beloved, and some suggest Sotha Sil was at times equally public.

Early in their reign, Almsivi faced major threats and crises. One of the first tests was an attempted vengeance by Ash King Wulfharth, who raised an army and storm to destroy the Tribunal, but the unified Dunmer under Almsivi repelled him. Almsivi also guided the Dunmer through the Middle Dawn crisis, with traditions describing signs in the heavens and protective wards against harm. Mannimarco later listed Almsivi among those able to identify their location during the Dragon Break.

In 1E 2703, the Tsaesci of Akavir passed through Morrowind during their invasion toward Cyrodiil. The Tribunal and Reman aligned forces to defeat the invaders. After victory, Reman integrated many Tsaesci veterans into his armies and personal service.

title: Almalexia — The Lady of Mercy and Divine Protector of Morrowind
text:
Almalexia, known as the Lady of Mercy, wielded her divine power for the protection and benefit of the Dunmer for thousands of years. While Sotha Sil remained distant and mysterious, and Vivec often took a philosophical role, Almalexia actively walked among her people throughout the First and Second Eras. She was widely regarded as compassionate, protective, and deeply involved in the daily lives of her followers.

Her blessings were said to perform extraordinary miracles. It was believed that her grace could protect individuals infected with Corprus from suffering its worst effects. Saint Felms the Bold claimed to be guided by her voice. Her personal guard, the Hands of Almalexia, were considered among the greatest warriors in Tamriel. Unlike Vivec, whose writings were metaphysical and complex, Almalexia composed moral fables and works intended to nurture virtue among the Dunmer.

In 1E 2920, long before the Oblivion Crisis of the Fourth Era, Mehrunes Dagon manifested and destroyed the city of Mournhold. Almalexia and Sotha Sil confronted him in open battle. After an immense struggle amid fire and devastation, they defeated and banished the Daedric Prince. This event demonstrated that Almalexia was capable of directly combating and overcoming a Daedric Prince centuries before the Empire would later face Dagon during the Oblivion Crisis. Some accounts suggest she foresaw in dreams both the end of the Four Score War and the eventual fall of the Reman Dynasty.

In 2E 572, Almalexia fought during the Akaviri invasion of northern Tamriel. She battled alongside Wulfharth, also called the Underking, against Ada Soom Dir Kamal. Accounts differ on details. Some sources claim she summoned the Underking, while others credit the Greybeards. Some state the battle occurred at Stonefalls, others at Red Mountain. Regardless of location, the invasion was repelled.

Following this conflict, Almalexia strongly supported the formation of the Ebonheart Pact, persuading most Great Houses except Telvanni to join. During the Alliance War of 2E 582, she suppressed the Maulborn cult in Deshaan, who sought to overthrow the Tribunal and restore Daedra worship. Their leader, Magistrix Urili Vox, had once served Almalexia but turned against her. The rebellion was crushed, reinforcing Almalexia image as protector and divine ruler of Morrowind.
